newsitem.title: USA: ITT to acquire Goulds Pumps for $815 million.
newsitem.headline: ITT to acquire Goulds Pumps for $815 million.

text.p: Industrial products maker ITT Industries Inc. will acquire Gould Pumps Inc. for $37 a share, or about $815 million in cash, plus assumption of $119 million in debt under a definitive agreement announced Monday.

The announcement, made before financial markets opened, pumped up Gould's stock, which surged $13.125, or 57 percent, to $36 in active trading on Nasdaq market, where it was the biggest percentage gainer.
ITT Industries, a widely diversified manufacturer of industrial products, will become a leading global supplier of pumps with the acquisition of Goulds, which is based in Fairport, N.Y.
Goulds Pumps is a worldwide supplier of industrial, residential and commercial pumps, parts and accessories. The company, which employs more than 5,200 people, had revenues of $774 million last year.
"On the revenue side, the products of ITT Industries' fluid technology business and Goulds complement each other perfectly," ITT Industries Chairman Travis Engen said in a statement.

"For example, Goulds is one of the leading producers of pumps for the industrial sector while White Plains, N.Y.-based ITT Industries is a world leader in submersible pumps for municipal water treatment worldwide," Engen said.
ITT Industries said it expects the acquisition to enhance earnings growth, "with an accretive impact in its first full year and significant contributions thereafter."
The cost benefits will result from greater economies in purchasing, manufacturing, marketing and sales, R&D and support functions, the company said.
ITT Industries stock rose 12.5 cents to $23.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Goulds also announced a "poison pill" shareholder rights plan as an anti-takeover defence. It said it would terminate the plan immediately before ITT Industries acquires the company.
Engen said in an interview he was unaware of any rival suitors for Goulds. He said his company approached Goulds in March.

In addition to pumps, ITT Industries subsidiaries make automotive brake and chassis systems, electronic warfare systems, radar equipment and valves. It was created in 1995 when ITT Corp. split into three companies.
